record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Two-step walk asymmetry on colored tori
record.original_question: Let T_n^k be the k-dimensional discrete torus, and color its vertices red and blue with exactly half of the vertices in each color. Let p_R be the probability that a random walk started from a uniformly random red vertex stays in the red class for at least two steps, and define p_B analogously for blue. For dimensions k ≥ 3, which pairs (x,y) in [0,1]^2 can occur as (p_R, p_B)? In particular, is the attainable region the convex hull of {(0,0)} together with the points (l/(2k), l^2/(2k)^2) and (l^2/(2k)^2, l/(2k)) for k ≤ l ≤ 2k?

evidence.quote: Our main question is: what happens for k ≥ 3? A tentative conjecture is that the answer is the convex hull of the set: {(0, 0)} ∪ {(l/(2k), l^2/(2k)^2) : k ≤ l ≤ 2k} ∪ {(l^2/(2k)^2, l/(2k)) : k ≤ l ≤ 2k}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $k\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2$, let $T_n^k=(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^k$ denote the $k$-dimensional discrete torus, viewed as a $2k$-regular graph in which each vertex $v$ is joined to the $2k$ vertices $v\pm e_i$ for $i=1,\dots,k$ (where $e_1,\dots,e_k$ is the standard basis). Assume $n$ is even so that $|T_n^k|$ is even. A balanced 2-colouring of $T_n^k$ is an assignment of one of two colours, red ($R$) or blue ($B$), to each vertex so that exactly half of the vertices are red and half blue.

Given a balanced 2-colouring, perform a simple random walk: from a vertex $v$, move to each of the $2k$ neighbours with probability $1/(2k)$. Define
$$p_R \;=\; \Pr\big(X_1\in R \text{ and } X_2\in R \;\big|\; X_0 \text{ is uniformly random in } R\big),$$
$$p_B \;=\; \Pr\big(X_1\in B \text{ and } X_2\in B \;\big|\; X_0 \text{ is uniformly random in } B\big),$$
where $(X_0,X_1,X_2)$ are the first three steps of the simple random walk on $T_n^k$.

For each fixed $k\ge 3$, characterise the set
$$\mathcal{A}_k\;=\;\overline{\bigcup_{n}\bigl\{(p_R,p_B)\in[0,1]^2 : (p_R,p_B) \text{ arises from some balanced 2-colouring of } T_n^k\bigr\}}\subseteq[0,1]^2.$$

In particular, decide whether $\mathcal{A}_k$ equals the convex hull of the set
$$\{(0,0)\}\;\cup\;\Bigl\{\bigl(\tfrac{\ell}{2k},\tfrac{\ell^2}{(2k)^2}\bigr) : k\le \ell\le 2k\Bigr\}\;\cup\;\Bigl\{\bigl(\tfrac{\ell^2}{(2k)^2},\tfrac{\ell}{2k}\bigr) : k\le \ell\le 2k\Bigr\}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A 2023 paper (updated 2025) by Gray and Johnson titled "Asymmetry of 2-step Transit Probabilities in 2-Coloured Regular Graphs" addresses this question. They fully characterize the attainable region for the 2-dimensional torus, give a general upper bound (the region lies in a certain polygon $D_{2k}$) for all dimensions, and provide partial constructions for higher dimensions, but the conjectured characterization for $k\ge 3$ remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Asymmetry of 2-step Transit Probabilities in 2-Coloured Regular Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization given for the 2-dimensional torus; only partial results and bounds for higher-dimensional tori.
status_evidence.claim: For k>=3 the conjecture characterizing the attainable region of (p_R,p_B) on the k-dimensional torus remains open.

status_evidence.title: Asymmetry of 2-step transit probabilities in 2-coloured regular graphs (ScienceDirect)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version addressing 2-step transit probability asymmetry on regular graphs including tori.
status_evidence.claim: The published treatment resolves the planar torus case but leaves the higher-dimensional conjecture open.
